summary: End-to-end verification of the new Stealth Decoy/Fake-Phone + Protection Status Checklist on the public preview (mobile 390x844, dm_device_id pre-seeded via addInitScript). All required behaviours verified except one natural-trigger limitation flagged below. (1) DECOY RENDERS when trapLevel>=2 -> DecoyMode (data-testid 'decoy-mode') shows fake home/clock + 8 fake apps (decoy-app-messages/photos/contacts/notes/phone/camera/weather/settings); the real security-dashboard is HIDDEN. Verified by stubbing /api/security/score via XHR addInitScript to return trap_level=3, waiting through the 18s guard interval. On entry the backend received intruder_photo + trap events (intruder_photo x2, trap x4). Tapping decoy-app-messages opened the in-app fake messages list (decoy-app-open) and logged actions to /trap/log-action. (2) OWNER EXIT: tapping decoy-statusbar-time x5 opens decoy-exit-modal -> wrong code '9999' shows 'Incorrect code' and stays in decoy -> correct code '4321' returns to security-dashboard with decoy-mode unmounted. (3) FRESH DEVICE NOT DECOYED: a brand-new device (no extreme baseline) unlocked with 1234= shows the real dashboard and STAYS on the dashboard after a 40s wait (no false alarm). (4) PROTECTION STATUS CHECKLIST: tile-status on the dashboard opens security-checklist-screen showing all 9 items (check-location/camera/notifications/phone/bluetooth/admin/sim/email/decoy). 'Decoy mode active' has a green tick. Web-only items show 'Fix' buttons (fix-location, fix-camera, fix-notifications, fix-admin, fix-email). Native-only items (Phone/Bluetooth/Device Admin/SIM) correctly display 'Needs the installed Android app'. (5) REGRESSION: setup -> cover (calculator) -> access code (1234=) -> dashboard flow still works. Bottom nav present (Home/Recovery/Evidence/Mate).

minor.issue: When the live in-app session sends pin_ok=true + screen=home (trained) + no lat/lng (headless) + behaviour features mismatched against an EXTREME baseline (typing_speed 520 etc.), the additive weighted trust still floors at ~0.55 (Monitor band, level=1), not the ~0.30 (Trap band, level=2) implied by the test spec. Reason: weights (behaviour 25, location 25, known_device 20, pin 15, app_usage 15) -> in headless we only get behaviour(0) + pin(15) + app_usage(~1)= 30/55 = 0.545. The natural in-app trigger needs at least one additional factor to drop (location away from home OR known_device=0 OR screen out of trained set). The Decoy gate itself works correctly once trap_level>=2.

ui_bugs.issue: The 'Protection Status' tile (tile-status) lives near the bottom of the home grid; its lower half is overlapped by the fixed bottom-nav (z-[10000]). A normal centre-tap at viewport y~799 lands on the bottom Home button instead of the tile. Programmatic dispatch_event clicks succeed, and the user can reach the tile by scrolling, but on a small viewport (390x844) the tile sits half under the nav by default. Recommendation: add pb-24 (or matching) to the dashboard scroll container so the last row of tiles fully clears the nav.

integration_issues.issue: App.js renders DecoyMode only after the next /score response inside the guard setInterval (18s). The initial post-unlock telemetry.score() at line 123 does NOT call setTrapLevel, so even if the very first score returns trap_level=3, the decoy appears 18s later. Consider also calling setTrapLevel from the immediate score() so the UI reacts within a few seconds of unlock.

action_items: Add bottom padding (e.g. pb-24) to the dashboard tile grid so tile-status fully clears the fixed bottom nav on 390x844.

Wire the immediate post-unlock telemetry.score() to setTrapLevel(r.trap_level) so the decoy can engage within ~2-5s of unlock instead of waiting one full 18s guard cycle (matters when an intruder unlocks with a stolen/coerced code).

Tune /score weights or the in-app payload so that an intruder using a trained screen with pin_ok=true can still reach the Trap band when behaviour is wildly off — e.g. either reduce pin weight (15 is high when pin is reachable to anyone post-cover), or have telemetry.score() omit pin_ok after N seconds, or boost the behaviour weight when behaviour similarity is near zero. Otherwise the headline decoy feature can be sidestepped in the most common scenario (thief who knows the access code or just unlocked it).
Consider clearing localStorage dm_device_id from the cover screen for QA; not blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js guard loop (lines 98-120) correctly debounces the dangerous side-effects (capture/notify) behind refs, AND resets them on level==0. The decoy suppression flag (decoySuppressed) also resets on level 0, which is correct because the recognised owner returning to Normal band should not silently suppress future decoy episodes forever.

DecoyMode.js correctly: (a) logs 'entered_decoy' on mount, (b) captures front-camera photo + location once via a ref guard, (c) routes every fake-app tap through log() to /trap/log-action, (d) supports the 5-tap hidden owner-exit on the status-bar time with a 2.5s window reset. Looks clean.

SecurityChecklist.js correctly distinguishes web vs native: native-only items get na=true on web and render a slate grey badge + 'Needs the installed Android app' hint. The Decoy item is hardcoded ok=true with no Fix button — matches spec.

App.js line 123 calls telemetry.score() immediately on unlock but does NOT propagate the result into setTrapLevel. That means a first-reading Recovery-band thief still waits ~18s before being trapped. Easy fix.

App.js decoy gate is `trapLevel >= 2 && !decoySuppressed` — correct. Note that decoySuppressed only resets on level==0 (Normal band), so an intruder who gets the owner to exit decoy once, then triggers it again in the same session, WILL re-enter decoy after the suppressed flag is cleared by a Normal-band reading. Good.

Decoy event metadata stored in MongoDB uses type='trap' with metadata.action — backend security_engine appears to log via _log_event correctly (4 trap events observed). Just confirm /evidence and /trap/log-action API serialises metadata.action so the front-end Evidence Center can render the action names.
tile-status overlap with bottom nav is a real UX bug that will block a non-trivial fraction of users from ever reaching the Protection Status checklist on a small phone. Should be one-line CSS fix.

success_rate.backend: 100% on observable endpoints (setup, telemetry, score, events, verify-access, trap/log-action, evidence/photo) — only weighting concern noted
success_rate.frontend: 100% on Decoy gate, decoy apps, exit modal (right+wrong code), fresh-device-not-decoyed, Protection Status checklist (9/9 items + 5/5 Fix buttons + native-only labels). One UX/UI bug on tile-status overlap with bottom-nav.

test_credentials: Disposable TEST_dm_iter12_* devices created per scenario via /api/security/setup. Decoy device access_code 4321 / fresh device 1234. Recovery rec22, wipe wip33, phrase 'find my phone', trusted +15551234567.
seed_data_creation: 3 disposable TEST_dm_iter12_* devices (decoy via XHR stub, fresh, checklist) — all prefixed TEST_ for cleanup. No production data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Important learnings for future runs: (a) The spec's expectation that EXTREME-baseline training alone is enough to push trust into the Trap band in a headless web session is OPTIMISTIC — pin_ok=true + screen=home (trained) + no location data still floors trust at ~0.545 (Monitor). To trigger the decoy naturally in headless, ALSO send screen='unknown_screen' or set known_device=0 with a profile that had it trained. Otherwise stub /api/security/score in addInitScript to return trap_level=3 (XHR-patch shown in iteration_12 script) and wait one full 18s guard cycle to observe the decoy. (b) The post-unlock immediate score does NOT set trapLevel — only the 18s setInterval does, so always wait at least 22s. (c) tile-status on the dashboard is half-covered by the fixed bottom-nav on 390x844 — use locator.dispatch_event('click') or scroll, otherwise a force-click hits the Home nav button instead. (d) Decoy exit: 5 taps on decoy-statusbar-time within 2.5s opens decoy-exit-modal; modal does not auto-close on wrong code. (e) Native checklist items (phone/bluetooth/admin/sim) deliberately show red on web — not a bug.
rca of the issue: Spec deviation #1 (natural-trigger): with pin_ok=true after the cover-code unlock, screen=home (trained), and no location signal in headless, trust = (25*0 + 15*1 + 15*1) / 55 = 0.545, which puts trap_level at 1 (Monitor), not the 2 (Trap) needed to render the decoy. Mitigation: lower pin weight, or omit pin_ok after a few seconds, or include behaviour-zero penalty. Spec deviation #2 (UX): tile-status overlap with bottom-nav — fix with pb-24 on the dashboard scroll container. Spec deviation #3 (latency): initial post-unlock score doesn't set trapLevel — wire setTrapLevel into App.js' immediate telemetry.score() call to react within ~2-5s.
